lab_title: Structural Anatomy and Circulation of the Human Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the human heart in 3D space.
Trace the exact path of blood through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Explain the relationship between ventricular myocardial thickness and the resistance of the circuits they pump to.
Understand the mechanical role of heart valves in maintaining unidirectional blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient the student to the external structure of the heart and the major vessels entering and leaving it.
key_visuals: A realistic, beating 3D human heart floating in the center of the AR workspace.
Clearly identifiable external vessels: Superior/Inferior Vena Cava, Pulmonary Trunk/Arteries, Pulmonary Veins, and the Aorta.
student_actions: Rotate the 3D heart model to view it from anterior, posterior, and lateral perspectives.
Select and highlight the major external vessels to reveal their names and whether they carry blood toward or away from the heart.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the internal anatomy of the heart, specifically focusing on the four distinct chambers.
key_visuals: A cross-sectional view of the heart (coronal plane) revealing the internal cavities.
Highlighted regions distinguishing the Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Left Atrium, and Left Ventricle.
student_actions: Toggle the cross-section view to look inside the heart.
Select each of the four chambers to read about its primary role in receiving or pumping blood.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the four heart valves, understanding their anatomical locations and their function in preventing backflow.
key_visuals: A close-up internal view focusing on the atrioventricular (tricuspid, mitral/bicuspid) and semilunar (pulmonary, aortic) valves.
Animated valves opening and closing in sync with the heartbeat.
student_actions: Use a slider to slow down the heart rate to better observe the valve mechanics.
Click on each valve (Tricuspid, Pulmonary, Mitral, Aortic) as it snaps shut to read how it prevents retrograde blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart and out to the pulmonary circuit.
key_visuals: Animated blue particles representing deoxygenated blood.
A glowing pathway starting from the Vena Cava, moving through the Right Atrium and Ventricle, and exiting the Pulmonary Arteries.
A schematic representation of lungs receiving the blood.
student_actions: Follow the path step-by-step by clicking on interactive checkpoints along the pulmonary circuit to trace the exact route of deoxygenated blood.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood through the left side of the heart and out to the systemic circuit.
key_visuals: Animated red particles representing oxygenated blood.
A glowing pathway starting from the Pulmonary Veins, moving through the Left Atrium and Ventricle, and exiting via the Aorta.
A schematic representation of the body (systemic tissues) receiving the blood.
student_actions: Activate the systemic blood flow animation.
Follow the path step-by-step by clicking on interactive checkpoints to trace the route of newly oxygenated blood as it is pumped to the body.

scenes.brief_purpose: Compare the myocardial thickness of the left and right ventricles and relate this structural difference to their functional pumping requirements.
key_visuals: A transverse (horizontal) cross-section of the ventricles emphasizing the thick muscular wall of the left ventricle compared to the thinner right ventricle.
Text labels indicating the relative resistance of the systemic versus pulmonary circuits.
student_actions: Use a virtual measuring tool to compare the thickness of the left and right ventricular myocardium.
Complete a drag-and-drop matching exercise linking the wall thickness to the distance blood must be pumped (lungs vs. entire body).

scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate all structures and pathways into a unified understanding of the dual-loop circulation and complete the lab with a summative assessment.
key_visuals: A transparent, beating 3D heart with simultaneous, continuous dual-loop circulation (blue and red particles flowing concurrently).
Holographic pins marking key structures without their labels.
student_actions: Observe the simultaneous nature of the cardiac cycle (both atria contracting, then both ventricles contracting).

Complete a spatial quiz by selecting the correct unlabeled holographic pin when prompted with a structure's name or function (e.g., 'Identify the valve that prevents backflow into the left ventricle').
